name: Caroline Polachek
label: Perpetual Novice
lede: A haunted-house idea in Boulder became a band, a Beyoncé credit and one iPod ad, before Caroline Polachek made the album Pitchfork ranked No. 2 of 2023.

eras.title: Tokyo, Connecticut, Boulder
eras.text: Caroline Polachek grows up between Tokyo and Greenwich, then starts a band in a Colorado dorm-town whose original plan was music for haunted houses. Two moves and one new member later, Chairlift is a Williamsburg band with a record deal.

years.h: Caroline Polachek is born in Manhattan
years.p: She spends ages one to six in Tokyo, then grows up in Greenwich, Connecticut.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives her father as a Chinese history scholar of Ashkenazi Jewish descent and her mother as of Scottish and English heritage. The Tokyo years are one line in her bio, but fans trace a lot of her later pop-and-elsewhere taste back to them.

years.cap: Caroline Polachek performing live in Bristol, UK - May 29th, 2023 · Wikimedia
years.h: Boulder: Polachek and Aaron Pfenning start Chairlift
years.p: Two University of Colorado students meet up in October 2005 with a plan to make background music for haunted houses.
years.xp: That is the origin as Wikipedia gives it: Pfenning and Polachek, University of Colorado Boulder, October 2005, haunted-house background music. The haunted houses never came. A band did.

years.h: The Daylight Savings EP starts in Los Angeles
years.p: Chairlift begin recording at New Monkey Studio with bassist Kyle McCabe. In August they move to Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

years.h: [[Patrick Wimberly|5708b562-3880-4be8-9dab-f2bb2834fbf8]] joins, then Kanine Records signs them
years.p: Wimberly completes the three-piece; the band signs to Kanine Records in June 2007.
years.xp: Wimberly would outlast one founder and become the other half of Chairlift's second act. He went on to produce for Beyoncé, Solange, MGMT and Blood Orange, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: An iPod ad does the marketing
eras.text: A debut album on a small label, one song in an Apple commercial, and a major-label reissue. Then one founder leaves for a solo project and Chairlift becomes a duo.

years.h: Does You Inspire You · Kanine debut
years.p: Britt Myers produces the first Chairlift album; Pitchfork gave it 5.6, Metacritic lands on 68.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Pitchfork scored it 5.6/10 and Prefix 7.5/10, and NME singled out its 80s arrangements of flutes and chiming guitars. Robert Christgau marked a choice cut.

years.cap: Does You Inspire You (2008), the album that carried "Bruises".
years.src: Wikipedia: Does You Inspire You · Wikipedia: Caroline Polachek
years.h: "Bruises" turns up in an iPod nano commercial
years.p: Yahoo! News reported on September 16, 2008 that the ad gave Chairlift a boost.
years.xp: The song appeared in an Apple iPod nano commercial, and it became the thing Chairlift were introduced as for years. Wikipedia cites Yahoo! News's September 16, 2008 headline, "Chairlift Gets A Boost From iPod Nano Ad."

years.h: Columbia reissues the album with two extra songs
years.p: "Le Flying Saucer Hat" and "Dixie Gypsy" are added, plus an extended "Make Your Mind Up". The "Evident Utensil" video is up for a VMA in Breakthrough Video.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the album had sold 11,000 copies in the United States as of April 2009, a small number set against how many people had heard "Bruises" in an ad. The MTV nomination for "Evident Utensil" was at the 2009 Video Music Awards.

years.h: Aaron Pfenning leaves to make records as Rewards
years.p: Chairlift becomes Polachek and Patrick Wimberly.

eras.title: Something, and a Beyoncé credit
eras.text: The duo makes the record that critics rank, then Polachek and Wimberly help write a track on a Beyoncé album.

years.h: "Amanaemonesia" starts the Something rollout
years.p: "Sidewalk Safari" follows in October and "Met Before" in November.

years.h: Something · Dan Carey and Alan Moulder produce
years.p: Pitchfork gives it 8, Metacritic 76; it debuts at No. 184 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: The album came out in the US on Columbia on January 24, 2012, with a UK release through Young Turks a day earlier. Polachek named Strawberry Switchblade, Bill Nelson, Yellow Magic Orchestra, OMD and Art of Noise as influences, alongside black metal and Japanese classical music. Stereogum ranked it ninth on its 50 best albums of 2012.

years.h: "Met Before" gets a choose-your-own-adventure video
years.p: Jordan Fish directs it; viewers steer the plot, and BuzzFeed ranked it among the year's best videos.

years.src: Crack Magazine: · Wikipedia: Caroline Polachek · Wikipedia: Patrick Wimberly
years.h: Polachek co-writes and co-produces "No Angel" for Beyoncé
years.p: Crack Magazine says the credit brought a Grammy nomination.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Polachek as co-writer and co-producer of "No Angel" on Beyoncé's 2013 self-titled album, with Wimberly co-producing. Crack ties her Grammy nomination to it. ABC News dates the nomination differently (2012), so it is treated cautiously here.

eras.title: A laptop in Rome, then Moth
eras.text: Polachek makes a solo record under a pseudonym, then Chairlift makes a third and last album.

years.h: Ramona Lisa: Arcadia, made on a laptop
years.p: She writes it at a Villa Medici residency in Rome and calls it pastoral electronic music.
years.xp: Wikipedia says she made the whole album on her laptop, recording vocals into its built-in microphone in hotel closets, airport gates and dressing rooms while touring with Chairlift. Pitchfork gave it 6.8; Under the Radar put it at No. 83 for the year and Dazed Digital at No. 18.

years.h: Moth · third and last Chairlift album
years.p: Written and produced by Wimberly and Polachek, with Robin Hannibal and Cecil Frena, at their Brooklyn studio.
years.xp: "Ch-Ching" came out October 14, 2015, then "Romeo", "Crying In Public" and "Moth To The Flame". Metacritic's score is 73; the album peaked at No. 7 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart. Rolling Stone called it "a record where love, music and love for music come together beautifully."

years.h: Chairlift announce they're done
years.p: A final tour follows in spring 2017.

eras.title: Under her own name
eras.text: A last tour, a second pseudonym, a feature on Charli XCX's mixtape, and then a record that finally says Caroline Polachek on the cover.

years.src: Wikipedia: Caroline Polachek discography · Wikipedia: Arcadia (Ramona Lisa album)
years.h: CEP: Drawing the Target Around the Arrow
years.p: Released on Pannonica, the Bella Union imprint that also put out Arcadia in Europe.

years.h: She guests on Charli XCX's Pop 2
years.p: Wikipedia notes she later appeared on Charli's Crash (2022) too.

yt: "So Hot You're Hurting My Feelings" (lyric video)
years.h: Pang · her first album under her own name
years.p: On her own Perpetual Novice imprint with The Orchard; Pitchfork 7.3, Metacritic 82, and No. 1 on Dazed's albums of 2019.
years.xp: Producers included Danny L Harle, Dan Carey, A. G. Cook, Jim-E Stack, Daniel Nigro and Andrew Wyatt. "Door" came first, on June 19, 2019, and "So Hot You're Hurting My Feelings" on September 16. Wikipedia reports that the latter reached RIAA Gold in 2024.
play: So Hot You're Hurting My Feelings

eras.title: Lockdown, Spain, and a run of singles
eras.text: A death in the family, a move to Spain with her main collaborator, and then two years of singles that build the next album in public.

years.h: Her father dies of COVID-19
years.p: Wikipedia and Crack both note it; she later relocates to Spain with Danny L Harle because of visa issues.
years.xp: Crack reports the visa issues and the move, and that she drew on flamenco and worked with Arca ("My favourite DJ in the world", she says). The record that came out of it was not built as a mourning album.

years.src: NPR: · Wikipedia: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You
years.h: "Bunny Is a Rider" is the first Desire single
years.p: NPR notes it gained traction on social media.
years.xp: The song opens a single run that includes "Billions", "Sunset", "Welcome to My Island" and "Blood and Butter". A behind-the-scenes clip from the video shoot is on YouTube.

years.h: "Billions": Pitchfork Best New Track
years.p: She and Danny L Harle wrote and produced it; Rolling Stone called it a trip-hop inspired, hallucinogenic epic.
years.xp: The Fader said it turned Pure Moods-era new age into something utterly splendid. It hit No. 4 on Gorilla vs. Bear's 2022 list and No. 14 on Slant's. The B-side reworked "Long Road Home", her collaboration with Oneohtrix Point Never.

yt: "So Hot You're Hurting My Feelings", Glastonbury 2022
years.h: Support slots with Dua Lipa and Megan Thee Stallion
years.p: ABC News says she toured with both; a video of "So Hot" at Glastonbury 2022 shows the size of the crowd she got.

eras.title: Desire
eras.text: The album that ended up No. 2 on Pitchfork's list, and a tour with a volcano.

years.cap: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You (2023)
q: She's an artist at the peak of her powers.
years.src: Wikipedia: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You · ABC News:
years.h: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You lands on Valentine's Day
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.7 and Best New Music, then ranked it No. 2 of 2023; Metacritic lands on 94.
years.xp:
Perpetual Novice, The Orchard and Sony released it. Wikipedia lists Danny L Harle, Dan Nigro, Jim-E Stack, Sega Bodega and Ariel Rechtshaid as producers, Grimes and Dido on "Fly to You", and Oneohtrix Point Never on "Long Road Home". It is her first album to chart across several territories: UK No. 23, US Billboard 200 No. 87.

The New York Times also put it at No. 2; DIY and Exclaim! named it No. 1. The 66th Grammys nominated it for Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical. Scores from Wikipedia's reception box.
play: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You

years.big: Ferocious, unhinged, comedic, sexy and an absolute mess
q: I'm a deep believer in what lies behind the story.
years.h: Pedro Almodóvar is on the mood board
years.p: Polachek's own words for the women in Almodóvar's films, a frame she took into Desire.
years.xp: Crack reports that the album grew from a song written during the Pang sessions in 2018 that didn't fit. Polachek says Harle didn't executive produce it because she had already begun writing, and adds: "We have so much faith in each other."

years.cap: Caroline Polachek performing live in Bristol, UK - May 29th, 2023 · Wikimedia
years.h: The Spiraling Tour: 70 shows and a smoking volcano
years.p: From Brighton on February 10 to Brisbane on December 13, with Radio City Music Hall on May 20.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Doss, Ethel Cain, Sudan Archives, George Clanton, Toro y Moi, Alex G and Magdalena Bay among the support acts, and the Sydney Opera House on December 4. Stage: a large volcano, smoke billowing from the top, and a cracked clock counting down a minute.

years.src: Wikipedia: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You
years.h: The Everasking Edition adds four songs
years.p: It includes Weyes Blood on "Butterfly Net".
